Listen to this article Share … vows to strengthen national unity Ahead of the 2027 Presidential election, President Bola Tinubu on Monday met with a cross-section of Igbo traders in Lagos to seek their support for his re-election bid Advertisement Advertisement The move, BusinessDay gathered, is to avoid a repeat of the results of the presidential election in 2023, where the President lost the state to his rival, Peter Obi, the then Labour Party presidential candidate The Labour Party standard-bearer’s victory in Lagos State was regarded as one of the most shocking results in the 2023 most astonishing aspect of the 2023 presidential election, as Obi scored 582,454 votes as against the 572, 606 scored by the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate. The event, which was held at the Wole Soyinka Cultural Centre, Lagos, was put together by notable Igbo sons and daughters serving in the administration of President Tinubu They include Dave Umahi, the Minister of Works; Doris Uzoka- Anite, Minister of State, Budget and National Planning; Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Minister of Foreign Affairs; Nkiruka Onyejiocha, former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, amongst others Tinubu, in his remarks, assured of his administration’s support for the Igbos who are mainly traders in Lagos The President urged the traders to feel free to apply for loans through the Bank of Industry Advertisement “All of you. Anyone in the business of trading can apply to the Bank of Industry. And get small-scale loans. ” The President expressed surprise at the large turnout of Igbos at the event and promised to support them with loans for their businesses Advertisement The President, who vows to continue to strengthen national unity, added that ” No one chose where he will be born “No one of us told God, when we were born, where we were born, what language we will speak. Whether Yoruba or Hausa. You have no control over it. It is God who created that opportunity. Advertisement Advertisement “Let’s see ourselves as one person. Living in the same house. Geographically called Nigeria. “So if you are in any position or anywhere, grow up there President Tinubu commended the traders for abandoning their source of livelihood to come to listen to him The President, who described his job as very challenging, said he was running back to Abuja to answer the call of duty ” It is very, very challenging to do this job. To turn the economy around. So, I have to work hard. To make sure the economy improves. To ensure that your children are in school, eliminate crisis in the universities and ensure that our children are all in school “Because they are poor doesn’t mean that they must not go to university. The university is stable today because we are doing well” He also urged the traders to massively mobilise their members to turn out en masse on election day ” I am ready to serve. On January 16, you must play your part. One man, one vote. One woman, one vote “You know the job. You know how to do it. We go close market that day “The day of election, no market. You know there is no market? Governor Babajide Sanwo-olu of Lagos, in his remarks, assured the President that the entire people of Lagos are united to vote for him ” The Igbo nationals and all of us are together. This is one Lagos. It goes to show that we are united. We are united as a people. We are united as citizens. “We are united for you. Because this is one time where all of us, irrespective of what part of Lagos we live in, that we have said using the Igbo community, come January 16, 2027, we will ensure that you have a number that you have never seen in Lagos before. “You are a completely detribalized Nigerian. You are a nationalist who will sing and will continue to be happy. Because what you have done for this country, you have done development in all spheres of endeavour. Sanwo-Olu said the developmental policies have touched every part of the country: “the north, in the east, in the south, and in the west. You have even done development in Lagos. And that’s why they all can come here and be happy” “The investment, the growth that we have seen in the last couple of years is second to none. And we want to thank you. The stability that you have given the market, the current direct investment we continue to see, and the growth of our youth, of our children, in all of the craft, in all of the spheres of life” Tony Nwabueze, President of the Igbo traders, while commending the President for the town hall meeting, assured that the Igbos are now ready to back his re-election bids He, however, pleaded with the President to provide loans for the traders at a single-digit interest rate to enable them to diversify into manufacturing and expand their businesses “His Excellency, the governor, has promised that he will honour the terms of this marriage. The incoming governor has also promised to uphold the agreement. “Above all, our father and leader, President Tinubu, has endorsed this relationship. “When you enter into a marriage and sign a marriage certificate, what more could you ask for? Baba, we thank you. Baba, we thank you. “We promise you that we have learnt our lessons. We, the market people, will stand with you, support you and honour every agreement we enter into today. “Baba, God bless you. Baba, God bless you. Baba, God bless you. “The market people from Alaba to Trade Fair and Ladipo are asking for one thing, Your Excellency. ” We are asking for the opportunity to empower our young people through single-digit interest loans. We want to move from importation to manufacturing, and we cannot achieve that without access to loans at five per cent interest. “We promise you, Your Excellency, that we will organise our members. If any of us is given a loan, we will cross-guarantee one another. If anyone defaults, those who stood as guarantors will take responsibility for the repayment.” Related News CAC, NiRA move to link business registration to free .ng domains, target dollar outflows Nigeria’s electricity crisis: Enough of excuses; Nigerians deserve reliable power Afreximbank targets €240bn factoring market to close Africa’s $300bn SME financing gap Advertisement Share You Might Also Like Fani-Kayode dismisses recall claims, says relations with S’Africa remains cordial Sheikh Sunusi Khalil’s case: Justice, political tensions and the need for restraint Obi raises alarm over alleged plot to link him to IPOB Advertisement Advertisement × Download the BusinessDay App Scan to download
